He is a freshman at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in the [[United States]], and has been labeled a top international prospect for the [[NBA]].{{cite web|title=13 - Steven Adams|url=http://nbadraft.net/players/steven-adams|work=nbadraft.net|accessdate=May 29, 2013}} == Early life == His father Sid Adams was an [[English people|Englishman]] who settled in New Zealand after serving in the [[Royal Navy]]. Steven was the youngest of Sid's 18 children with five different women; his mother is [[Tongan people|Tongan]]. Steven's siblings and half-siblings are notable for their unusual size and athletic prowess. Adam's brothers average 6'9" (2.06 m), and his sisters average 6' (1.83 m).{{cite news|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/sports/pitt-big-east/pitt-big-man-steven-adams-backstory-is-as-interesting-as-his-future-is-intriguing-656568/ |title=Pitt big man Steven Adams' backstory is as interesting as his future is intriguing |first=Ray |last=Fittipaldo |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=October 7, 2012 |accessdate=December 11, 2012}} One of Adams' sisters is [[Valerie Adams]], NZ Olympic gold medal shot-putter. === Overcoming adversity === Adams has identified his father's death in 2006 as one of the defining events of his life. In a 2012 interview, Adams recalled:
When I lost my dad, that was a big hit for me. I didn't have that parental guidance, and I kind of took advantage of it because I was a stupid idiot. I decided not to go to school a couple of times, go when I felt like it. I always lied to my brothers and sisters. They'd ask: 'Are you going to school?' I'd say 'yeah.' They eventually found out.
One of his brothers, Warren,{{cite web|title=Steven Adams, UPitt Profile|url=http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111111aaa.html|accessdate=June 11, 2013}} stepped in to fill the gap, inviting Adams to move from his hometown [[Rotorua]] to [[Wellington]] and live with him. The brother placed him in a local basketball academy, and the head of the academy arranged for him to attend [[Scots College, Wellington|Scots College]]. Although some commentators in New Zealand believed Adams would not qualify to play for [[College basketball|college ball]], he did well enough to qualify academically to play in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]]. ==Basketball== ===High school career=== After graduating from [[Scots College, Wellington|Scots College]] in December 2011, Adams enrolled at [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Preparatory School]], a well-known basketball prep school in [[Fitchburg, Massachusetts]], for one semester. He was rated as the number 6 player in the [[ESPNU]] 100 class of 2012.{{cite web|title=Steven Adams|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/117483/steven-adams|publisher=ESPN.com|accessdate=12/5/2012}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|15=no|collapse=no|year=2013}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Steven Adams | position = C | hometown = Rotorua, New Zealand | highschool = Notre Dame Preparatory School | feet = 7 | inches = 0 | weight = 250 | commitdate = 7/5/2010 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} |} ===Professional career=== ====New Zealand==== In [[2011 New Zealand NBL season|2011]], Adams played for the [[Wellington Saints]] in the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|NBL]].{{cite web|title=Player statistics for Steve Adams|url=http://www.sportingpulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&client=11-8336-114272-159868-15173978&pID=192372016|work=SportingPulse.com|accessdate=May 17, 2013}} Adams won the Rookie of the Year award, and helped Wellington to win the NBL championship over the [[Hawke's Bay Hawks]]. Adams left New Zealand in January 2012 to enroll at Notre Dame Preparatory School. ====NBA Draft==== On April 2, 2013, Adams declared for the [[2013 NBA Draft]] which will take place on June 27 at the [[Barclays Arena]] in Brooklyn, New York. Adams is regarded as a late lottery pick to mid first round selection. If he is selected in the first round of the draft, he will be the first New Zealander to ever be selected in the first round of an NBA Draft. He would also be the first player out of Pittsburgh to be selected in the first round since 1999 when [[Vonteego Cummings]] was selected by [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 26th overall pick.[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/8503912/Kiwi-Steven-Adams-declares-for-NBA-draft Kiwi Steven Adams declares for NBA draft] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Steven_Adams/222926 Profile] at Eurobasket.com *[http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111111aaa.html College bio] {{Persondata | NAME = Steven Adams | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = New Zealand basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = 28 July 1993 | PLACE OF BIRTH = Rotorua, New Zealand | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Adams, Steven}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:New Zealand basketball players]] [[Category:New Zealand people of English descent]] [[Category:New Zealand people of Tongan descent]] [[Category:People from Rotorua]] [[Category:People from Wellington City]] [[Category:Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball players]]
